questions.question: What are variables and types in Ruby?
questions.title: Variables and Types in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Ruby is dynamically typed: a variable's type is its current value; you don't declare types. x = 42 (Integer); x = 'hi' (now String). Core types: Integer, Float, String, Symbol, Array, Hash, Range, Boolean (true/false), nil. Variable scopes by prefix: local (x), instance (@x), class (@@x), global ($x), constant (UPPER). Everything is an object — 42 has methods (42.times), nil does (nil.nil?), even classes are objects (Class). Check a type with x.class or x.is_a?(Integer). Ruby favors duck typing: if an object responds to the methods you call, use it — don't check its class. Assignment is by reference for objects (a = []; b = a; b << 1 changes a too); copy with dup/clone for a shallow copy. Use .frozen? to check immutability. Variables are labels pointing to objects; reassigning points the label elsewhere.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Checking types with == (use .class or duck typing), or assuming assignment copies (it's a reference for objects).

sections.title: Variables and types
sections.content:
```ruby
# Dynamic typing (no declarations; type = current value)
x = 42        # Integer
x = 'hi'      # now a String
x.class        # String  (check a type)
x.is_a?(Integer)  # false

# Core types:
42              # Integer
3.14            # Float
'hi'            # String
:name           # Symbol
[1, 2]          # Array
{ k: 'v' }       # Hash
(1..5)          # Range
true, false     # Booleans
nil             # no value

# Variable scopes (by prefix):
local_x = 1                # local
class Box
  @@count = 0              # class variable
  MAX = 10                 # constant (UPPER)
  def initialize; @x = 0; end  # @x: instance variable
end
$global = 1               # global (avoid; use sparingly)

# Everything is an object (even numbers/nil/classes):
42.even?                  # true
nil.nil?                  # true
Class.class               # Class  (classes are objects too)

# Duck typing: don't check the class; call the method.
def speak(x); x.sound; end   # works for Dog, Cat, anything with .sound

# Assignment is by REFERENCE for objects:
a = []
b = a
b << 1
a                         # [1]  (a changed too!)
c = a.dup                 # shallow copy (independent)
c << 2
a                         # [1]  (a unchanged)

# frozen?: immutable check
'x'.frozen?               # false (usually)
```
